## Scale

  - check: {"type":"question","q":"A light-year is a unit of what?","options":["Distance: how far light travels in a year","Time: one year","Brightness","Speed"],"answer":0,"feedback":[null,"It has the word year, but measures distance.","Brightness uses magnitude.","Light moves at a constant speed; the light-year is how far it goes."],"explain":"Light travels about 9.5 trillion kilometres in a year.   - check: {"type":"question","q":"Which unit suits the distance from Earth to the Sun?","options":["Astronomical unit (AU)","Light-year","Metre","Kilogram"],"answer":0,"feedback":[null,"A light-year is far too large here.","A metre is far too small: the number would be huge.","A kilogram measures mass, not distance."],"explain":"One AU is the average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km.   - check: {"type":"question","q":"The Sun is about 1.5 × 10^8 km from Earth. Written out in full, that is:","options":["150 000 000 km","15 000 000 km","1 500 000 000 km","1.5 million km"],"answer":0,"explain":"10^8 is 100 million, so 1.5 × 10^8 is 150 million."}

tasks:
  - check: {"type":"sort","q":"Which line of evidence is it?","options":["Redshift","CMB","Matter proportions"],"items":[["Distant galaxies are moving away from us","Redshift"],["A faint glow reaches us from every direction","CMB"],["About three-quarters of the mass is hydrogen, almost all the rest helium","Matter proportions"],["The universe is expanding","Redshift"],["The early universe was very hot and has cooled","CMB"],["Hydrogen and helium nuclei formed in the first few minutes","Matter proportions"]]}

```teacher
summary: A self-test on the scale of the universe, the CMB and matter
  proportions, and how the lines of evidence fit together (AC9S10U03, nodes 1, 4
  and 5, taught in class; node 5 a hinge).
time: 16
timing: Node 1 6 min · Node 4 5 min · Node 5 5 min
goals:
  - I can order the parts of the universe by scale and use light-years and AU.
  - I can say what the CMB and the hydrogen-helium mix show.
  - I can say why several independent lines of evidence strengthen a theory.
before: >
  A Quick check: a few questions on what students should know for AC9S10U03
  nodes 1, 4 and 5, which you teach in class. It has no board, no clip and no
  new teaching, and it is optional, so it never holds up course completion. Set
  the width with `?width=minimum`, `typical` (default) or `wider`.


  Use it as a self-test after your teaching, a starter, or revision. The big
  bang and redshift lessons are on screen (nodes 2 and 3). A scale activity (a
  class-sized solar system, or a number line) and a discussion of dark matter
  work better in the room.
running:
  - "Node 1: have students place objects on a scale line before the questions."
  - "Node 5: ask which line of evidence they would show a sceptic first, and
    why."
struggle: Holding the sizes in mind. When a student mixes light-years and
  kilometres, ask what the distance would look like in each.
stuck:
  - see: A student says a light-year is a length of time.
    ask: What does light do in a year?
    fix: It travels. The light-year is the distance it covers.
  - see: A student says the big bang was an explosion in space.
    ask: Where was the space?
    fix: Space itself expanded. There was no outside to explode into.
stretch: How long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth (about 8 minutes)?
  Use it to place one AU on a scale in light-minutes.
support: Give the scale list on cards to order, with a unit sheet (AU, light-year).
leads: >
  Back in class: a model of the expanding universe (dots on a balloon);
  discussion of what is still unknown.
exit:
  q: Name two lines of evidence for the big bang and what each shows.
  a: "Redshift: the universe is expanding. CMB: it was hot and dense early. (Or
    hydrogen and helium proportions.)"
explain: >
  The universe is organised from planets and stars up to galaxies. Distances use
  **astronomical units** (inside the solar system) and **light-years** (between
  stars).


  Three **independent** lines of evidence support the big bang: **redshift**
  (expansion), the **cosmic microwave background** (a hot early universe) and
  **matter proportions** (hydrogen and helium). Their agreement makes the theory
  strong, though questions such as dark matter remain open.
```
